title: Seeing God
lead: "No human being can see me and stay alive" (Exodus 33:20), yet Jacob, Moses, the elders, Isaiah and Ezekiel meet God in ways the Bible calls seeing. The New Testament says no one has seen God, but the Son has made him known (John 1:18), and promises that the pure in heart will see him (Matthew 5:8; Revelation 22:4).

sections.b: Hagar names God "El-roi, God who sees" (Genesis 16:13), and Jacob says he saw God face to face at Peniel and lived (Genesis 32:30). The elders of Israel see the God of Israel and eat and drink (Exodus 24:9–11), yet Moses is told no one can see God's face and live (Exodus 33:20), though God speaks with him "mouth to mouth" (Numbers 12:8). Isaiah cries out that he is lost because his eyes have seen the King (Isaiah 6:5), and Ezekiel sees only "the likeness of the glory of the LORD" (Ezekiel 1:28). The New Testament says no one has seen God, but the Son has made him known (John 1:18), and whoever has seen Jesus has seen the Father (John 14:9). It promises that the pure in heart will see God (Matthew 5:8) and that his servants will see his face (Revelation 22:4).
